### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, every one of the 200 traces contained A01, A02 and A03; A03 ran about 2.1 times per trace and repeated within the same trace in roughly 55 in 100 traces. In the later window, none of these three activities is observed in any trace. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, POS001, POS002, POS003]
- A04 shows the mirror image: it is not observed at all earlier, while later it appears exactly once in every one of the 200 traces. [OCC004, POS004]
- A05's successor changed completely: earlier, A05 was followed by A02 in all 200 traces; later, A05 is followed by A04 in all 200 traces. [DIR003]
- A08's outgoing flow changed: earlier it led to A03; later, about 46 in 100 of its outgoing transitions go to A06 and about 54 in 100 to A07. A03's own outgoing split (about 53 in 100 to A06, about 47 in 100 to A07) disappeared together with A03. [DIR002, DIR004]
- A06 and A08 remain optional in both windows, present in about 55 in 100 traces earlier and about 50 in 100 later, and they still run before or interleaved with the downstream activity (A01 earlier, A04 later). [REL005, REL007, REL020, REL022]
- A07 remains mandatory in both windows but sits earlier in the trace: its mean relative position moves from about 0.48 to about 0.30. [POS006]
- Among the disappearing activities, A01 and A02 always co-occurred with A02 first, and A03 co-occurred with both, either before them or interleaved during its repeats; later, neither member of these pairs is ever present. [REL001, REL002, REL008]
- The downstream order is preserved around the new activity: A05 before A04 and A07 before A04 in all later traces, mirroring A05 and A07 before A02 and A01 earlier. [REL019, REL021, REL004, REL006, REL010, REL012]
- Event distances shifted about one step earlier: A06→A07 from lag 3 to lag 2, A08→A07 from lag 2 to lag 1, A06→A05 from lag 4 to lag 3, A08→A05 from lag 3 to lag 2, and the self-repeats of A06 and A08 from lag 3 to lag 2. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG006, LAG007]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that the block formed by the repeating A03 and the chain A05 → A02 → A01 is no longer executed and has been replaced by a single execution of A04: A01, A02 and A03, previously present in every trace, are unobserved later; A04, previously unobserved, now runs exactly once per trace; and A05, which previously fed into A02 (onward to A01), now leads directly into A04. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, DIR003]

The rerouting is seen directly in the successor profiles (A05→A02 versus A05→A04, and A08→A03 versus A08→A06/A07), while the preserved order of A05 and A07 before the end activity and the roughly one-step-earlier distances are all coherent with A03 and A02 dropping out of the flow rather than with a mere shift in path frequencies. [DIR003, DIR004, REL019, REL021, LAG001, LAG003, LAG004, LAG006]

Screening qualified 43 control-flow items where only about 0.24 would be expected by chance alone, so the body of evidence is far beyond what an unchanged process typically produces. [screening]

Limitations: zero participation only means an activity was not observed in that window, many items describe the same underlying traces and are not independent confirmations, and the evidence cannot rule out that the two windows sample different case mixes or process variants rather than one modified process. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]

Other differences: A06 and A08 occur slightly less often (about 55 in 100 traces earlier, about 50 in 100 later), and A07's mean relative position moved earlier (about 0.48 to 0.30); these shifts, together with the one-step-earlier lags, are consistent with the same restructuring rather than separate changes. [POS005, POS006, REL005, REL007, LAG001, LAG003, LAG004, LAG006]
